children: Daiichi Life's bid to take full control of Australia's Challenger makes strategic sense to UBS analysts. Lowering their recommendation to neutral from buy, they tell clients in a note that Daiichi's local subsidiary is Australia's largest life insurer. A combination with the country's largest annuity provider would increase capital efficiency, enhance Challenger's domestic capabilities including in fixed income, and offer stronger long-term structural growth for the Japanese company. That said, the offer of 11.80 Australian dollars a share still lags the UBS analysts' estimated fundamental value. UBS raises its target price by 6.5% to A$12.25. Challenger shares are up 0.2% at A$11.77. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
